answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money. 2. Each player has one active worker on the notepad and three inactive workers lying on the reserve spaces. 3. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 as hand cards, and discard 4 face up. 4. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 5. Put Action card Animals in the leftmost slot (strength 1); randomly place the other four cards in the remaining slots; all start side I up. 6. Appeal starts at 0 for the start player, then 1, 2 and 3 in turn order.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C1–F: 25 money; one active and three lying workers; draw 8/keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards. Animals under leftmost slot; appeal staggered 0–3.

answers.answer: 1. Two players place 3 face-up Base Conservation Project cards; three players also place 3; four players place 4. 2. Only in a two-player game, block one level on each of the three face-up projects (left on the left card, middle on the middle, right on the right) and block the three spaces in the donation area's left column; both players cannot use those spaces. 3. The summary gives no additional blocked spaces for three- or four-player games. 4. Reveal the six-card display after every player has chosen their hand cards during setup.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c: 4 projects in a 4-player game, otherwise 3; 2-player blocked levels/donation spaces. Setup F–G: reveal display after hands are chosen.

answers.answer: 1. After using a card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were left of its empty slot one place right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before performing the action; each X-token spent adds 1 strength and returns to the supply. X-tokens gained during that action cannot boost it. 3. You may spend any number of X-tokens, but may hold no more than 5. 4. Resolve an “after finishing” effect after the action is complete, including moving its Action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove used card, shift cards left of empty slot right, put it in slot 1; strength set before action; each X adds 1; maximum 5; after-finishing follows card movement.

answers.answer: 1. You may not take a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings; you may not do nothing. 2. Instead, select an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token, then move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards as usual; its strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3. You cannot take this alternative if you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: may not do nothing; X-token action specifies exactly one, card movement, irrelevant strength/upgrade, and five-token limit.

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore extra steps beyond it; the break occurs after the current turn ends. 2. The player who reached the last space gains 1 X-token. 3. The triggering player finishes the current turn, then the break takes place; after the break play continues clockwise with the next player. 4. The summary does not describe an extra turn caused by a break trigger itself; the separate game-end rule grants final turns if the end is triggered.
answers.evidence: Break track: reaches last space, break after current turn, 1 X-token, ignore extra steps. Break procedure continues clockwise with next player.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces without money, then choose either a deck draw per the strength table (maximum 3, with a possible discard) or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 display card of your choice regardless of reputation. 2. Cards II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or from folders within reputation range in any order per the upgraded table; snapping exactly 1 display card is available from strength 3, and snapping has no reputation restriction or deck draw. 3. Cards II display cards are not replenished until the whole turn ends. 4. On either side, display refill after a snap is at turn end; there is no in-turn hand limit, and hand size is enforced only at breaks.
answers.evidence: CARDS action: both sides advance 2; side I draw/snap at 5; side II draws within range and/or deck, snap from 3; display replenished at end turn; hand limit only at breaks.

answers.answer: 1. Reputation range includes the display folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Reputation 10 or higher requires the upgraded Cards action. 3. At reputation 15, further reputation stays at 15 and gives 1 appeal per additional reputation step. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track: within range means matching folder plus lower folders; 10+ requires Cards II; at 15 overflow becomes appeal; discard pile cannot be inspected.

answers.answer: 1. Build I makes exactly 1 building, size at most action strength; pay 2 money per space. Build II may build any number of different buildings with total size at most strength, but never two identical buildings in that action. 2. Your first building must cover at least one border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 3. Build only on empty spaces within the map; do not overlap buildings or cover water/rock spaces. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 4. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 5. Each pavilion immediately and only once gives 1 appeal.
answers.evidence: Build action: side I exactly one; side II multiple different up to total strength. Placement rules; kiosk distance; pavilion gives appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Build I allows standard enclosures sizes 1–5, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo per zoo (size 3). 2. Build II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary per zoo (each size 5); each special enclosure type has four tiles in supply. 3. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 4. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 appeal; Build II allows restricted-icon spaces to be covered, though the full-map reward can also trigger from other effects.
answers.evidence: Buildings table and Build description: four tiles per special type, one each per zoo; unique buildings only via Sponsors; full map gives 7 appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action. 2. Pay for each item before receiving that item's own benefits. 3. Resolve immediate effects as they arise; defer effects explicitly marked “after finishing” until the entire action and Action-card movement are complete. 4. If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: earlier action bonuses can be used later, items paid before their own benefits, and after-finishing after card movement. Summary says owning player chooses simultaneous-effect order.

answers.answer: 1. For each animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its full cost, and house it legally; matching-continent partner zoos reduce cost by 3 money per continent icon, so two such icons reduce it by 6. 2. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the animal's required size; flip the whole enclosure to its occupied side, normally housing one animal. Required water/rock adjacency must be satisfied, counting distinct adjacent terrain hexes. 3. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use their special enclosure; mark the indicated occupied spaces with one player token per space, and never flip a special enclosure. 4. Effects after an animal play usually resolve immediately before the next animal; “after finishing” effects wait until the Animals action and card movement finish. Pay full cost before any money-gain effect from the play.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS: conditions, payment, partner discount per icon, housing, distinct terrain adjacency, special-enclosure tokens, and effect timing.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II lets you play animals from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; an animal taken from the display costs extra money equal to its folder number. 2. At strength 5+, you may optionally gain 1 reputation at the very beginning, so the raised range can apply to animals played in that action. 3. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. 4. Animals II permits animals with an upgrade-required condition.
answers.evidence: Animals II: display animals within range, folder-number extra cost, optional reputation first at strength 5+, no refill until turn end, upgrade-conditioned animals allowed.

answers.answer: 1. Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you relocate all corresponding eligible animals that fit, deciding separately for each; this is once per newly built building. The special enclosure must satisfy each animal's water/rock requirements and have enough capacity. 2. Mark each moved animal's indicated special-enclosure spaces with that many player tokens from your supply; the Reptile House and Aviary each have 5 spaces. 3. For each animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including terrain. If none does, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting size alone; if none meets even size, flip none.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals: only at construction; all suitable animals that fit; capacity and adjacency; flip smallest meeting all requirements, fallback by size, otherwise none.

answers.answer: 1. Association tasks have strengths: increase reputation 2, gain partner zoo 3, gain university 4, conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task, with at least one active worker and action strength at least the task value. Association II performs one or more different tasks, totaling no more than action strength. 3. If one of your workers is already on a task, you must place 2 workers to repeat it; if 3 of your workers are already there, it is unavailable until after the break. 4. Other players' workers on a task do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association action: task values and side I/II limits; worker repetition rules; other players' workers do not matter.

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from the available tiles on the Association board and put them on the lowest empty corresponding space on your map; take any printed covered-space bonus immediately. A university's own reputation award is also immediate. 2. You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents. 3. You may have at most 4 partner zoos, and the third/fourth requires Association II. 4. A matching partner zoo discounts animal costs by 3 per matching continent icon and supplies that continent icon. 5. Only the hand-limit university raises the hand limit from 3 to 5; the other universities do not change it.
answers.evidence: Association partner zoo/university tasks, board source, lowest space and bonuses; limits and hand-limit university table.

answers.answer: 1. Association I project work may support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II may also play it from the in-range display, paying the folder number. New projects go above the board, leftmost, shifting existing projects right. 2. Support a condition with no player's token on it, meet its requirement and place one player token from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition. You may support a given project only once; each reward level can hold only one token total across players. 3. Removing your map token activates its bonus, taken immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice; recurring-marked bonuses repeat each break. 4. If a new card exceeds the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to their owners' supplies, not their map edges; their bonuses stay activated.
answers.evidence: Association conservation project work, support limits and token source; bonus timing; overflow discard and token destination.

answers.answer: 1. A Release into the Wild animal must match the project's printed standard-size category, not exactly one size: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. 2. Before conservation is gained, lose only that animal's printed appeal, discard the animal and lose its icons; keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. 3. Playing a new Release project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. 4. If the animal can live in a special enclosure and its required tokens can be removed, remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, falling back to the smallest meeting size alone, or none if none meets size.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild project rules: size categories, loss/retention, play reputation, and special-token/standard-enclosure freeing procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I may play exactly one hand Sponsor if action strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Sponsors II may play one or more cards, from hand and/or in-range display; action strength plus 1 must be at least their total levels, and display cards cost their folder number. 2. Resolve cards sequentially, fully resolving each card's instant effects (except after-finishing effects) before the next. 3. Instead of playing cards, Sponsors I advances the Break token by strength and pays that much money; Sponsors II's break option pays money twice that amount. The full money is paid even if the token has fewer remaining spaces than the strength.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action: side I and II budgets/source/cost/timing; break-token money options and full payout despite reaching final space.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit (3, or 5 with hand-limit university); clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock eligible partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Kiosk income is 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count, but empty special enclosures do. 3. If multiple players take display cards during income, resolve clockwise beginning with the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise); refill display after each such player before the next chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6 and kiosk-income/display-card income ordering.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or an available Bonus tile. At 10, the first player to reach or exceed it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if nobody reaches 10, everyone discards one before scoring. 2. End is checked at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed one another; appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your own turn end or a break unless another player triggers the end first. 3. After an own-turn trigger, the triggering player completes the turn and all others take one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation. VP equals Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive VP wins; tie goes to most supported projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: conservation milestones, end timing and final turns, 4-point per-card cap, VP formula and tiebreak.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the 9 Bonus tiles and place one face up on each of four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 and two beside 8. Do not place tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons; return the remaining five tiles to the box. 2. If a component supply runs out, use a suitable substitute; physical stock alone does not forbid a legal play, although per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Setup: random tiles on four blank spaces beside 5/8; other five unused. Component supply rule says use suitable substitute.

answers.answer: 1. Maps 1–8 are advanced maps. Choose 2 random zoo maps and select 1 advanced map, or lay out player count + 1 advanced maps and choose in reverse play order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A begins with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on indicated spaces; the printed kiosk is covered by a tile as a reminder and counts as built.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A: advanced-map selection methods; Map A ability includes empty 3-space enclosure and kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. Each player's seven support tokens start on the designated spaces along the left edge of their zoo map; the rest stay beside the map. Taking a support token activates its associated bonus. 2. Hire inactive workers from the lowest reserve space upward. 3. Some maps reward conservation points when you hire your last worker; the summary does not specify a universal reward amount because it depends on the map.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2; Association worker supply edge case; Full-throated clarification for last-worker map reward.

answers.answer: 1. On upgrade, flip one chosen Action card from side I to side II in its current slot. 2. Its improved action is usable starting with your next action, but it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. 3. You cannot upgrade all five Action cards; four upgrade opportunities exist and one offers an alternative choice.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards: flip one in place; side II from next action; immediately counts upgraded for conditions; four upgrade ways and cannot upgrade all.

answers.answer: 1. At strengths 1 through 5, Cards I draws respectively 1, 1, 2, 2, 3 cards and discards respectively 1, 0, 1, 0, 1. 2. A required discard may be one of the newly drawn cards or a card already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw table: Side I draw/discard 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1; required discard may be new or held.

answers.answer: 1. The categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. Bear counts as a category even when also shown with herbivore or predator; Petting Zoo animal is its own category. Include both special categories unless explicitly excluded.
answers.evidence: Animal categories and Base glossary shared principles list all seven and clarify bear/Petting Zoo animal inclusion.

answers.answer: 1. Donation is available only with Association II, after performing at least one Association task in that same action; it needs no worker and is limited to one donation per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible, cover that donation space with a player token from your supply, and gain 1 conservation. 3. Costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all but the last are covered, further donations cost 12 and place no additional token.
answers.evidence: Association II donation rule: one donation after a task, smallest visible cost, supply token, 1 conservation, listed cost sequence and repeatable last space.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements. Left-side play conditions and Conservation Project icons are not zoo icons. 2. A card counts its own icon for effects; doubled icons count twice. 3. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Base glossary shared principles: icon sources/exclusions; card counts own icons; doubled icons count twice; card text priority.

answers.answer: 1. Terrain adjacency counts distinct water or rock hexes that touch the enclosure/building; multiple edges touching the same terrain hex count once, while a larger region contributes only the hexes actually adjacent. 2. Connected terrain regions do not change this distinct-hex count. 3. Water/rock illustrations printed on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not satisfy requirements.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes; larger area only adjacent hexes; tile illustrations provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

answers.answer: 1. The player who plays a new Release into the Wild project gains 1 reputation; a player who later supports a project already in play does not gain that play bonus. 2. Breeding Program projects 123–127 use the same requirement for all three reward spaces; choose any available space that is unoccupied and whose condition you fulfill.
answers.evidence: Release project rules specify new card grants reputation, later support does not; Breeding Program has same requirement all three spaces and choose any available.

answers.answer: 1. For X:Y, X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward. 2. A condition with no number or with “per” pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; where multiple thresholds exist, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: X:Y reading, condition without number/per, numbered thresholds and highest threshold.

answers.answer: 1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map and personal supply; “any zoo” includes those for all players.
answers.evidence: Base glossary definitions of connected, isolated, border, your zoo and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. Unique buildings are placed when their Sponsor is played; they have no size-based building payment. 2. Use the matching tile, colored face up, and rotate freely but do not flip it; follow ordinary placement rules and any printed water/rock adjacency. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house extra animals, and are not terrain spaces. 3. If the tile cannot legally fit, the Sponsor card cannot be played.
answers.evidence: Base glossary unique-building rules: placement, orientation, payment, ordinary/terrain restrictions, and inability to play card if placement impossible.

answers.answer: 1. Finish the Animals action, including moving the Animals card to slot 1, before taking a granted Action. Then use that Action card normally and move it to slot 1 afterward. 2. A named action such as Sponsors cannot be replaced by the X-token alternative; Determination (Any Action) may choose the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Action/Determination timing and movement; named action exclusion versus Determination option.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion or Dominance searches the unused face-down Base Conservation Project deck; Assertion takes the chosen project and Dominance takes its named project into hand. Return the deck afterward. 2. Dominance has no effect if its named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediately support the card through Association above the board; it does not join the setup base-project row below.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion/Dominance source, no effect if already in play, later placement above board.

answers.answer: 1. Resolve Boost or Clever after finishing Animals and moving that card. 2. Clever puts the chosen Action card in slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. 3. Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or slot 5; moving it to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Boost/Clever timing and slot movement.

answers.answer: 1. An affected zoo must have at least 5 appeal for Constriction, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Venom. 2. The played animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its interactive effect; its new appeal normally need not count when selecting affected players. 3. The group may replace interactive abilities with the card's solo alternative text without playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities: eligibility floor 5; animal appeal may be awarded either order; multiplayer replacement option.

answers.answer: 1. Constriction tokens go on the affected player's highest-numbered Action-card slots: one token on slot 5 for a target ahead on one track, or two tokens on slots 4 and 5 for a target ahead on both Appeal and Conservation. 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Each token reduces that action's strength by 2, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 4. Return a token after the marked card is used, or remove it without effect at the break.
answers.evidence: Interactive target table and Constriction clarification: slot placement/count, no stacking, strength reduction and removal timing.

answers.answer: 1. At effective strength zero or below, a constricted card cannot perform its regular action unless you spend enough X-tokens to raise it to at least 1; it may instead take the alternative X-token action. 2. You may also leave it until it is at least in slot 3, where its slot strength may permit use.
answers.evidence: Constriction: at effective strength 0 or below, boost to at least 1, use X-token alternative, or leave card until at least slot 3.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 gives up to two selections; after each card, decide again whether to discard a display card and replenish it or discard a hand card and draw one from the deck. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replaced immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification: up to twice; decide again after each; display discard replenished immediately with folders shifted.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal may avoid flipping an empty enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least its standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore may host any number of flock animals. 3. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, it still frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure; exact historical residents need not be tracked or proven.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification: qualifying host and reuse, normal housing/future non-flock rule, release procedure and no historical resident tracking.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad, where it can be used immediately. 2. Take a last-worker map reward if shown. 3. If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated: activate lowest reserve worker; take map reward if shown; no effect if all workers active.

answers.answer: 1. Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards and adds one revealed Animal card to hand, discarding the rest. If no Animal card appears, discard all revealed cards.
answers.evidence: Hunter X clarification: reveal X; keep one Animal and discard others; if no Animal, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Hypnosis chooses among tied players with the highest appeal and at least 5 appeal; if you are the highest-appeal target, it has no effect. 2. Copy only a target Action card in slot 1, 2 or 3; use that card's owner's side/upgraded status for the action, and spend your own X-tokens. 3. Move the borrowed card to slot 1 normally. 4. Venom and Constriction on that card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Interactive target table; Hypnosis details on ties, self target, slots, target-side upgrade, own X-tokens, movement and tokens.

answers.answer: 1. Place a gained Multiplier immediately on its named Action card; a bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card. On its next use, execute the action twice in succession at the same base strength, and move its Action card only after both executions. 2. Each X-token boosts only one execution; defer after-finishing effects until all executions finish. 3. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn is finished and does not stop the second execution. 4. Return used Multiplier tokens to supply; an unused one is removed at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier rules: placement, two executions, X-token per execution, effects and break timing, token return/expiry.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens allow up to three executions, not four. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative can take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but cannot mix one X-token action with one regular action.
answers.evidence: Multiplier clarification: each additional token adds an execution; two gives three; alternative action may be multiplied but cannot mix regular and X-token actions.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking lets you place a Large Bird Aviary before Build II, provided your zoo does not already have one and a legal site exists. 2. Other placement rules still apply, including Build II for upgrade-marked spaces. Posturing also follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
answers.evidence: Peacocking and Posturing clarifications: Aviary exception, legal site, restricted spaces, normal placement and sequential placements.

answers.answer: 1. Petting Zoo animal appeal rewards are 3 for the first, 6 for the second and 9 for the third. 2. One Petting Zoo holds at most three of these animals. 3. They count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal clarification: first/second/third appeal; single Petting Zoo max three; count as small.

answers.answer: 1. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; Pilfering 2 separately targets a highest-appeal zoo and a most-conservation zoo, each with at least 5 appeal. 2. Choose among ties; the most-conservation target must have at least 1 conservation. If the same zoo qualifies twice, it is targeted twice. 3. A self-target has no effect.
answers.evidence: Interactive target table and Pilfering X clarification: target selection, ties, minimum conservation, repeat same target and self-target.

answers.answer: 1. The target chooses to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. With no hand cards, the target gives money; with less than 5 money, the target gives a card. With neither a card nor 5 money, the target gives all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated Pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X: target choice, no Final Scoring cards, shortage rules and sequential resolution.

answers.answer: 1. Cards tucked under an animal by Pouch have no remaining function; if that animal is released, discard its tucked cards too, while keeping appeal already earned from tucking. 2. Cards sold through Sunbathing go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarifications state tucked-card handling, retained appeal, and discard destination for sold cards.

answers.answer: 1. An extra Final Scoring card drawn before the 10-conservation milestone joins your choices when you discard one card at that milestone. 2. At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card; each card is separately capped at 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance clarification: extra card joins discard choice; score every remaining card, each with four-point cap.

answers.answer: 1. Scavenging shuffles the discard pile face down, draws randomly from it, makes the card's stated selection, then returns the discard pile face up. Scavenging 3 draws three random cards, keeps one and discards the others.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification: shuffle face down, random draw, selection and return face up; illustrated Scavenging 3 behavior.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; it does not draw from the deck instead. Sponsor Magnet looks for display Sponsor cards, which need not be within reputation range; if none are present, it does nothing. 2. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping and Sponsor Magnet clarification: exact source and count, reputation treatment, empty result and refill.

answers.answer: 1. Venom tokens are placed on the affected player's lowest-numbered slots in order (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; return duplicates. 2. Using a card with Venom removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn; using the alternative X-token action also removes one if you have fewer than 5 X-tokens. 3. Pay 2 money at turn end only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one remains on your cards. If unable to pay, undo the turn and choose another action; you cannot avoid the fee by spending all money. 4. Unused tokens clear at the next break without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom X clarification: placement/duplicates; use and fee condition; inability to pay; break expiry.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian gives immediate money based on universities: 2 money for 1 university, 5 for 2, and 10 for 3. 2. It reduces the strength required to support conservation projects from 5 to 4. 3. Its final-scoring reward is 1 conservation for having three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 203 Veterinarian.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough counts previously supported projects by the number of support tokens missing from the left edge of your map and gives 2 appeal per such project. 2. It gives 1 conservation at every break.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 206 Medical Breakthrough.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research counts different continent and animal-category icons; for each two, it gives you 1 conservation. 2. Every other player gets 2 money per conservation point you gain.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 207 Basic Research.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon immediately. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation if you have five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 208 Science Library.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon immediately. 2. Each Americas icon played lets you build one free kiosk, following normal placement and kiosk-spacing rules. 3. Its final condition is five or more kiosks, rewarding 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 210 Expert on the Americas.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon immediately. 2. Each Australia icon played lets you tuck one hand card beneath this Sponsor for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 212 Expert on Australia.

answers.answer: 1. Each card puts two supply tokens on itself. When supporting a Base Conservation Project below the Association board, return exactly one token as any one icon; never use both tokens on the same support. 2. Projects that originated as base cards but were played above the board do not qualify. 3. Final scoring gives 1 conservation with five or more project supports, counted by tokens missing from the left edge of your map.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 215/218 Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer allows each Build action to add one extra copy of a building built in that same action without extra strength; pay its normal money cost and obey placement rules. 2. Only one extra building is allowed, even if multiple different buildings are built. Special enclosures remain limited to one of each type per zoo. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map except water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 217 Engineer.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2. It permits covering water/rock spaces and ignoring terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; printed terrain icons still count. 3. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo; terrain need not be covered for a full-map condition. 4. Its final reward is 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 219 Diversity Researcher.

answers.answer: 1. Archaeologist triggers when you receive an actual placement bonus on a border space. 2. For each such trigger, choose any uncovered placement bonus on your map, whether or not it is on a border. 3. Multiple triggers may choose the same bonus or different bonuses, in an order you choose. 4. Its final condition is all building border spaces covered, excluding water/rock, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 221 Archaeologist.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. 3. You may repeatedly support the same release project with different qualifying animals, but only one token per project per Association action. Each token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 224 Migration Recording.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and select the next qualifying player. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation with all five continents.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 225 Quarantine Lab.

answers.answer: 1. Choose small or large permanently and mark that choice with a player token from your supply; reveal deck cards until finding an animal of that type, keep it and discard the rest. 2. You cannot play animals of the opposite type. 3. Chosen small animals gain 2 extra appeal, or chosen large animals gain 4; size-3 animals remain legal but receive no bonus.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 227 WAZA Special Assignment.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal immediately. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals lets you play one extra small animal from hand, with normal costs and rules; mixing small and large animals prevents the effect. 3. Then add one small animal from the display to hand regardless of reputation; you may take it even if you declined the extra play.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 228 WAZA Small Animals Program.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon immediately. 2. Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, even if several spaces belong to one building; a space adjacent to multiple water hexes pays only once. 3. Its final condition gives 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected (none isolated).
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 241 Hydrologist.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut places its unique building. 2. Each bird icon played triggers drawing two cards from the deck, keeping one and discarding the other.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 249 Barred Owl Hut.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank must be placed adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard the sold cards.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 250 Sea Turtle Tank.

answers.answer: 1. For each predator icon played, Spotted Hyena Compound triggers Hunter, with the number of revealed cards equal to your total predator icons. 2. A single card with two predator icons triggers Hunter twice in sequence, counting both new icons for the first trigger and then counting the updated total again for the second.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 252: each predator icon triggers Hunter using total icons; double-predator card triggers sequential Hunters, counting new icons each time.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable enters play with three supply tokens on its card. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token to play a Sponsor from hand. 2. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet normal conditions; the Sponsor source is hand. 3. The Stable's own herbivore icon can trigger this when the Stable is played, for up to three uses total.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 253 Okapi Stable.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation immediately. 2. Place its building covering at least two border spaces. 3. Then take one display card within reputation range or draw one deck card; resolve its simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 254 Zoo School.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance is placed on two border spaces and unlike ordinary buildings need not touch an existing building; later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break it gives 2 money per adjacent building, excluding empty standard enclosures; it may be beside a kiosk. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 257 Side Entrance.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals immediately gives 1 appeal per connected, uncovered building border space; water and rock are excluded. 2. At final scoring, gain 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluated separately for each group (the summary example groups 13, 6, 3, 2 yield 3 total). 3. Count upgrade-restricted spaces even if Build is not upgraded; exclude water/rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 260 Native Farm Animals.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon; research icons do not count. 2. Each continent/category newly introduced to your zoo gives 1 appeal and 2 money. 3. A double of the same new icon receives the novelty reward only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 262 Explorer.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place a size-5 standard enclosure free under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition, such as a required icon or Animals upgrade; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, which can ignore one condition, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference row 263 WAZA Large Animal Program.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares each animal category: gain 1 conservation for each category in which you have more icons than the player to your right. 2. If that player has no icons in a category, one of your icons is enough to lead it. 3. Maximum reward is 4 conservation.
answers.evidence: Final scoring clarification Biodiverse Zoo 009.

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower's bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. Housing an animal there grants the two appeal again even if an earlier animal was released and the enclosure emptied. 4. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1 Observation Tower clarification.

answers.answer: 1. A standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex qualifies; adjacency only to a different water hex does not. 2. It counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; a physical size-2 enclosure there is treated as size 4. 3. This cannot be ignored on release or transfer. 4. It does not affect special enclosures, and Outdoor Areas is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2 Outdoor Areas clarification.

answers.answer: 1. A building on Commercial Harbor's adjacent building space activates it; your first building may begin beside it but need not. 2. Its discard ability may be used before, during or after your action, once per own turn, never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 Commercial Harbor clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type, occupancy or whether several hexes belong to one building; empty enclosures qualify if covered. 2. The Restaurant is not a building and does not count as a kiosk neighbor. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and follow other normal placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5 Park Restaurant clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Cover Hollywood Hills H spaces with buildings under ordinary placement rules; each covered H reveals deck cards until a Sponsor appears, which you keep, discarding other revealed cards. 2. H is not a placement bonus, so it does not trigger Archaeologist. 3. Once all three are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Its partner bonuses still require Association II for a third/fourth partner, and building bonuses still require Build II on restricted spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 Hollywood Hills clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its usual conditions. 2. The Sponsor must come from hand, even with Sponsors II. 3. This effect leaves the Sponsors Action card in its current slot; it does not move it.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: pay Sponsor level, meet conditions, only from hand even with Sponsors II, Action card stays put.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; gains beyond those track ends are lost. Reputation has a separate overflow rule: after reaching 15, each further reputation gives 1 appeal.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: Appeal 113 and Conservation 41 caps; reputation overflow described separately.

answers.answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal. 2. Hypnosis targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal, with you choosing among ties; if you are the target, no effect, and it copies only slot 1, 2 or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-appeal zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal zoo and most-conservation zoo, with at least 5 appeal, ties chosen by you, and the conservation leader must have at least 1 conservation; self-targets have no effect. 4. Constriction affects every other zoo with at least 5 appeal ahead of you on Appeal and/or Conservation: one token if ahead on one track, two if ahead on both.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference and ability clarifications for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Constriction.

answers.answer: 1. For an Animal card, a partner-zoo condition means a partner zoo from the specified continent; for a Sponsor card, it permits a partner zoo from any continent. 2. A maximum-25-appeal condition allows play only while you have at most 25 appeal; the marker is a reminder, not a general track cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed value. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one left-side requirement, such as a required icon; it does not remove terrain requirements.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ on partner-zoo condition, max-25 appeal, minimum reputation, and ignore-condition bonus.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine Digging 2 offers up to two choices between (a) discarding one display card and immediately replenishing the display, or (b) discarding one hand card and drawing one deck card. 2. You choose again after each selection, so the two choices need not match.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification: choose up to twice between the two specified options and decide again after each card.

answers.answer: 1. After display cards are taken, move cards from higher-numbered folders down in order, preserving their order, then fill empty spaces from the deck. 2. The summary specifies this for end-of-turn refill; it does not separately detail an alternative ordering for final empty folders beyond filling them from the deck.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display: move higher-numbered folders down keeping order, then fill empty spaces from deck.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. A covered placement-bonus space gives its bonus immediately once; turning the enclosure occupied later does not award that placement bonus again.
answers.evidence: Build action opening: standard enclosure empty side up; placement bonus immediately once; no second award when later occupied.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches 10 conservation, each player chooses and discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile.
answers.evidence: Conservation 10 milestone: all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; turns proceed clockwise. Play has no formal rounds: players take turns one at a time, with breaks between turns when triggered. 2. On a regular turn, take one action using one of the five Action cards. Resolve the action and then move the used card; additional effects or bonuses follow their timing, including after-finishing effects after card movement.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly determine start player, clockwise. Overview: no formal rounds, one turn at a time; turn structure specifies one Action card action.
